verdict.rationale: Rive documents RML, an XML text-based representation of a Rive file that lets developers create and modify Rive content as code outside the Editor. Its open-source runtimes also load and parse .riv files, which makes the format toolable to a degree. However, no published spec for the .riv binary format is evidenced, and a community member notes the open runtime still requires the Rive Editor to author content. Missing for 10: a documented or open .riv format specification, evidence that RML round-trips to .riv without the vendor editor or CLI, and independent hands-on corroboration of portability.

support.subject: As a developer, the file format is open or documented, so my designs stay portable and toolable outside the vendor's editor

citations.quote: Rive Markup Language (RML) is a text-based representation of a Rive file. It lets you create and modify Rive content as code
making it possible to build Rive files with coding agents and other text-based workflows instead of working exclusively in the Editor
RML uses XML to describe the objects and relationships in a Rive file
The Rive runtimes are open-source libraries that allow you to load and control your animations in apps, games, and websites.
Loads .riv files, advances state machines and animations, and draws via the abstract Renderer interface.
